title: SYSK Selects: How Lewis and Clark Worked
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2013 episode "How Lewis and Clark Worked," introduced by Josh as a pick for this week's Select. The hosts cover the Louisiana Purchase that set up the expedition, Jefferson's goals, the preparation of Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, and the crew including York, Sacagawea, Jean Baptiste (Pompey) and the dog Seaman. They trace the route up the Missouri, winter at Fort Mandan, the Shoshone horse trade over the Continental Divide, the Columbia River, the Pacific coast and Fort Clatsop, and the return trip with its violent encounters. The episode ends with the expedition's aftermath: York's unfulfilled hopes for freedom, Lewis's death in Tennessee, and the lasting debate over manifest destiny. A listener mail segment about a Dutch diplomatic immunity arrest closes the show.
topics: Ken Burns Lewis and Clark documentary

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick, a 2013 episode on how Lewis and Clark worked. The hosts joke about shared surnames and compare the Ken Burns documentary on the expedition.

segments.title: Louisiana Purchase and Jefferson's expedition idea
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Louisiana Purchase, in which Monroe bought the territory from Napoleon for about three cents an acre, and how it made the Lewis and Clark expedition a mission to claim and survey new land. Jefferson's goals included finding a water route to the Pacific and cataloguing the region.

segments.title: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark's preparation
segments.summary: Lewis was Jefferson's private secretary and chose Clark as co-captain. They discuss Lewis's personality and depression, and rumors about his sexuality, which the hosts say have no evidence. Lewis trained in Philadelphia with the American Philosophical Society in astronomy, medicine and other subjects.

segments.title: Members of the Corps of Discovery
segments.summary: The hosts describe York, Clark's slave who was a full member of the party and helped in diplomacy, and the Newfoundland dog Seaman. They discuss the crew's discipline problems and the discharges of two men. Another party member, Charles Floyd, is noted as the only person to die on the trip.

segments.title: Departure and Teton Sioux standoff
segments.summary: The expedition left St. Louis in spring and went up the Missouri River, hauling boats upstream. They met the Teton Sioux, who wanted to control trade, and a standoff over a canoe was defused by Chief Black Buffalo.

segments.title: Great Plains, Fort Mandan and Sacagawea
segments.summary: The expedition reached the Great Plains and built Fort Mandan near the Mandan and Hidatsa. They discuss syphilis among the party, hiring Toussaint Charbonneau and his wife Sacagawea, her role as translator, and the birth of her son Jean Baptiste.

segments.title: Wildlife, grizzlies and the Missouri fork
segments.summary: Past Fort Mandan, the party encountered prairie dogs, elk, buffalo and grizzly bears for the first time. They reached a fork in the Missouri and followed Lewis and Clark's choice against the majority, then Lewis realized they had crossed the Continental Divide.

segments.title: Great Falls portage and Shoshone horses
segments.summary: The party took a 53-day portage around the Great Falls, then reached the three forks and met the Shoshone. Sacagawea recognized a childhood friend and her brother, now chief, and the Shoshone guide Old Toby led them through the Bitter Root Mountains, where they ate horse meat.

segments.title: Columbia River, Pacific coast and Fort Clatsop
segments.summary: The party floated the Columbia River with Nez Perce help and left horses in their care. They reached the Pacific in November, and Lewis called the ocean tempestuous. They voted on where to winter, including York and Sacagawea, and built Fort Clatsop.

segments.title: Return journey, Blackfeet conflict and Coltrane
segments.summary: The party started home in March 1806 and retrieved their horses from the Nez Perce. They split up in July, and a violent encounter with the Blackfeet left two dead. Lewis was accidentally shot by Pierre Cruzatte. John Colter left to explore and is credited as an early visitor to Yellowstone.

segments.title: Return to St. Louis and aftermath
segments.summary: The expedition returned to St. Louis in September 1806 to cheers. They mapped the region and catalogued many species, and rewards were given to members, but York and Sacagawea received no land. Clark denied York's request for freedom. Lewis became governor of Upper Louisiana and died in Tennessee, with suicide and murder both disputed.

segments.title: Closing and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts close the expedition story and note that Clark and the rest of the party later lived out their lives. A listener email about the Dutch arrest of a Russian diplomat and diplomatic immunity is read. Closing plugs are given.
